description.narrative: The proposed program forms a cornerstone of the Government of the Philippines' strategy to achieve macroeconomic stability by fostering sound fiscal management, an enabling environment for the private sector, and resilience to climate change, as envisaged in the Philippine Development Plan (PDP) 2023-2028. Subprogram 1 lays the foundation for strengthening public financial management (PFM) systems for the ensuing, more targeted policy actions under subprogram 2 in line with the PFM Reforms Roadmap 2024-2028.

description.narrative: Output/s as listed by the project staff.

1.1. The government endorsed and submitted the Senate Bill on Budget Modernization which institutionalizes the Cash Budgeting System to promote fiscal discipline in the budget preparation, execution, and monitoring processes. (DBM)

1.2. The government enacted Republic Act No. 11966 on Public-Private Partnership (PPP) Code of the Philippines to: (i) integrate climate resilience, sustainability, and gender and development policies into PPP projects; (ii) uphold high standards of environmental and social safeguards; (iii) enhance bankability of PPP projects for private partners to provide a credible pipeline of projects; and (iv) ensure efficient risk allocation between the government and the private sector. (PPP Center)

1.3. The government approved Executive Order No. 29 to modernize public financial management (PFM) processes through the Integrated Financial Management Information System (IFMIS), to harmonize key PFM functions including budget management, budget execution, cash management, and accounting and reporting. (DBM)

1.4. The government approved Executive Order No. 31 to institutionalize the Open Government Partnership, an international platform of the national and local governments, and civil society organizations, to promote transparency and citizens participation in government processes through citizen access to budgetary data, thereby strengthening social accountability and empowering citizens. (DBM)

1.5. The government adopted the National Asset Management Plan (NAMP) which mandates the government agencies to digitalize asset records and implement the Asset Management System (AMS) to improve accountability, sustainability, and financial efficiency of government assets. (DBM)
